speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked the Minister for Law whether the Ministry will consider providing psychological and counselling support and legal advice for all bankrupts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: MinLaw’s Insolvency Office makes available to debtors and bankrupts user-friendly information on the bankruptcy process.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have noticed that a lot of bankrupts, especially the first timers, when they were made bankrupt, they are traumatised emotionally and also psychologically, and some of them even slip into depression.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In quite a lot of cases, they do not understand what is meant by being bankrupt.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As such, could the Ministry provide psychological support or counselling to all the first-time bankrupts?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We understand that it can be a traumatic, a novel experience even, for bankrupts to be in this situation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, whilst they are bankrupt, the Insolvency Office working with various social service agencies, as I had mentioned, and also agencies such as Workforce Singapore and NTUC's e2i in the context of assisting bankrupts with employment opportunities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, the Insolvency Office has also had the benefit of working with Singapore Polytechnic's Institute of Financial Literacy.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This tie-up helps to provide bankrupts with financial literacy courses to allow bankrupts to make plans whilst they are bankrupt, and also to look at the options available to them after they are discharged from bankruptcy so that they can organise and maintain their financial matters better.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, there is a range of different options, beginning with pre-bankruptcy for an individual who is in financial difficulty; and also, if they inevitably go into bankruptcy, there is a series of support options open for them to seek advice from and to try and find a way out of bankruptcy; and also, as I had mentioned, post-bankruptcy, how they can organise and maintain their financial matters better to avoid being in the same situation again.
